articles.title: Anthropic CEO Amodei admits "there's a huge uncertainty in what's going to happen next year" days before a record IPO
articles.summary: Days before what could be the largest IPO in history, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called buying compute 'the deepest business dilemma' his company faces. Anthropic's commitments now total nearly $901 billion, and it's still far from clear whether future revenue will justify those costs. The planned IPO is largely meant to serve as a financial buffer against that uncertainty. Anthropic and its investment banks are meeting prospective investors in New York, Boston and San Francisco to gauge demand for the offering, one of the people and a third person familiar with the matter said.

articles.title: Jensen Huang's ouster likely traces back to Nvidia's risky business practices more than his personal life
articles.summary: Jensen Huang likely left Nvidia more because of risky business practices than anything else, a Wall Street Journal report suggests. At the very least, those practices made him enemies internally. The company offered cloud providers billions in financial guarantees for chip purchases, including a planned $250 billion deal with OpenAI. Interim CEO and then-CFO Colette Kress tried to contain the risk, and Huang reportedly didn't like that. The article Jensen Huang's ouster likely traces back to Nvidia's risky business practices more than his personal life appeared first on The Decoder.

articles.title: Banks bar Chinese and Hong Kong investors from Anthropic IPO over US export controls
articles.summary: Chinese investors are shut out of Anthropic's IPO, Bloomberg reports. Banks are rejecting buy orders from mainland China and Hong Kong, citing U.S. export control rules known as ITAR. Similar restrictions applied during SpaceX's IPO, and Anthropic's products aren't available in either region anyway.
